About.title: About GloRe

intro.tagline: Give value to your volunteering experiences.
intro.body: GloRe is an open network of volunteering organizations that turns real experience into recognized competence. Volunteers learn and self-assess their soft skills online, a tutor from the host organization validates the result, and a personalized certificate documents the hours, tasks, and skills demonstrated.

mission.title: Our mission
mission.description: To give professional recognition to the soft skills people develop through volunteering, so non-formal learning counts as much as formal study.

vision.title: Our vision
vision.description: A world where every volunteering experience is valued, and where the skills it builds are visible to employers everywhere.

values.title: Our values
values.description: Openness, transparency, and trust. Recognition is free for volunteers, the network is open to organizations, and every certificate is validated by a real tutor.

network.title: Our network
network.description: An open network of volunteering organizations across Europe, Latin America, and beyond, working to consistent quality standards under a shared charter.

skills.title: Soft skills we recognize
skills.description: Courses are built around the transferable skills that volunteering develops.

contact.title: Get in touch
contact.description: Want to join the network or learn more? Reach out through your local partner organization or contact us at <email>info@glorecertificate.net</email>.
contact.coordinator: GloRe is coordinated by Associazione Joint, a Milan non-profit founded in 2003, with the support of the Erasmus+ programme.

About.description: GloRe, short for Global Recognition, turns volunteering and non-formal learning into a verifiable credential you can add to your CV.

story.title: Where GloRe comes from
story.description: GloRe began as an Erasmus+ Capacity Building project (2016 to 2018) led by Associazione Joint, a Milan non-profit founded in 2003 and active in youth mobility and European volunteering. It grew into the GloRe Network, an open, free-to-join set of NGOs across Europe and Latin America that issue certificates under shared quality standards.

howItWorks.title: How the certificate works
howItWorks.description: GloRe complements tools like Youthpass with a flexible, validated record of soft skills.

step1.title: Learn and self-assess
step1.description: Complete the skill courses for the competences you practised and rate your own level for each one.

step2.title: Qualify
step2.description: Once you have completed at least 3 skill courses with an average rating of 3 out of 5, you can request a certificate.

step3.title: Get validated
step3.description: A tutor from your organization reviews your levels and the activity details, then approves or asks for changes.

step4.title: Share a verifiable credential
step4.description: GloRe issues a PDF with the organization's signatory and a public page with a QR code, so anyone can confirm the certificate is genuine.

trust.title: Why it can be trusted
trust.description: Recognition only works if a third party believes it.

validation.title: Validated by a tutor
validation.description: Every certificate is reviewed and approved by a tutor from the issuing organization, who takes responsibility for its content.

immutable.title: Immutable once approved
immutable.description: After approval a certificate cannot be changed, so the record stays exactly as it was issued.

verifiable.title: Publicly verifiable
verifiable.description: A public page and a QR-linked PDF let employers and institutions confirm a certificate without contacting anyone.

volunteer.label: Volunteer
volunteer.intro: As a volunteer you learn soft skills, assess yourself, and earn a certificate validated by a tutor.

step1.title: Join your organization
step1.description: Accept the invitation from your organization, or open the invite link it shares. If the link needs approval, the organization confirms your request first. Then your courses appear on the dashboard.

step2.title: Complete skill courses
step2.description: Work through skill courses and their lessons. Each one ends with a final assessment that rates the skill from 1 to 5.

step3.title: Self-assess your skills
step3.description: Answer the self-assessment prompts honestly. Your ratings build the competence profile your certificate is based on.

step4.title: Request your certificate
step4.description: Once you qualify, submit a certificate for your volunteering experience. A tutor reviews it and either approves it or asks for changes.

q1.question: When can I request my certificate?
q1.answer: After you complete at least 3 skill courses with an average self-assessment of 3 out of 5 or higher. The button unlocks once you qualify.

q2.question: What is a self-assessment?
q2.answer: After a skill course you rate your own level on the skills it covers. These ratings form your competence profile and are confirmed by a tutor during review.

q3.question: What happens after I submit a certificate?
q3.answer: It is assigned to a tutor and moves to "In review", then to either "Approved" or "Changes requested". If changes are requested, edit and resubmit it.

q4.question: How do I join an organization?
q4.answer: You join through your organization. Someone from your organization invites you by email or shares an invite link, and some links need the organization's approval before you get in. If your organization is not on GloRe yet, a representative can apply to register it.

q5.question: I belong to more than one organization. How do I switch?
q5.answer: Use the organization switcher in the sidebar. Each organization is like a separate workspace, with its own courses, role, and certificates.

q6.question: Which languages are available?
q6.answer: The platform is available in English, Italian, and Spanish. You can switch language at any time from your account.

learner.label: Learner
learner.intro: As a learner you can take introductory and learner courses to explore soft skills at your own pace.

step1.title: Join your organization
step1.description: Accept the invitation from your organization, or open the invite link it shares. If the link needs approval, the organization confirms your request first.

step2.title: Explore the courses
step2.description: Open the introductory and learner courses available to you and work through their lessons.

step3.title: Track your progress
step3.description: Each lesson is marked complete as you finish it, so you can always pick up where you left off.

step4.title: Ask about certification
step4.description: Certificates are reserved for the volunteer role. If you want to certify your soft skills, ask your organization about becoming a volunteer.

q1.question: Why can't I request a certificate?
q1.answer: Certificates are tied to the volunteer role and to skill courses. Learners take introductory and learner courses. Ask your organization if you want to become a volunteer.

q2.question: What kinds of courses can I take?
q2.answer: Introductory courses explain how GloRe works, and learner courses are tailored to your path. Both let you explore soft skills without a final assessment.

q3.question: How do I join an organization?
q3.answer: You join through your organization. Someone from your organization invites you by email or shares an invite link, and some links need the organization's approval before you get in. If your organization is not on GloRe yet, a representative can apply to register it.

q4.question: I belong to more than one organization. How do I switch?
q4.answer: Use the organization switcher in the sidebar. Each organization is like a separate workspace, with its own courses, role, and certificates.

q5.question: Which languages are available?
q5.answer: The platform is available in English, Italian, and Spanish. You can switch language at any time from your account.

tutor.label: Tutor
tutor.intro: As a tutor you review the certificates assigned to you and decide whether to approve them.

step1.title: Find your assignments
step1.description: New certificates are auto-assigned to the tutor with the fewest open reviews. You can also self-assign any unreviewed certificate.

step2.title: Open the review
step2.description: Opening the review form moves the certificate to "In review". Check the activity details and the skills with their levels.

step3.title: Adjust if needed
step3.description: You can edit the activity dates, duration, location, description, and the skill levels so the certificate reflects what really happened.

step4.title: Approve or request changes
step4.description: Approve to generate the PDF, or request changes with a comment. The volunteer can edit and resubmit to you.

q1.question: How are certificates assigned to me?
q1.answer: New certificates are auto-assigned to the tutor with the fewest open reviews. You can also self-assign any certificate that has not been reviewed yet.

q2.question: What can I change during a review?
q2.answer: You can edit the activity dates, duration, location, and description, plus the skills and their levels, before you approve.

q3.question: What does approving do?
q3.answer: It generates the PDF, records the issue date, and makes the certificate immutable and publicly verifiable. The first approved certificate becomes the volunteer's default certificate.

q4.question: How do I join an organization?
q4.answer: You join through your organization. Someone from your organization invites you by email or shares an invite link, and some links need the organization's approval before you get in. If your organization is not on GloRe yet, a representative can apply to register it.

q5.question: I belong to more than one organization. How do I switch?
q5.answer: Use the organization switcher in the sidebar. Each organization is like a separate workspace, with its own courses, role, and certificates.

q6.question: Which languages are available?
q6.answer: The platform is available in English, Italian, and Spanish. You can switch language at any time from your account.

manager.label: Owner or representative
manager.intro: As an owner or representative you manage your members, approve join requests, and keep reviews moving.

step1.title: Review join requests
step1.description: People who open your invite link may need your approval. Review each request on the organization page and decide whether to let them in.

step2.title: Manage members and roles
step2.description: Invite members, change roles, and assign tutors. Volunteers earn certificates; learners take intro courses; tutors review.

step3.title: Keep reviews balanced
step3.description: Certificates are auto-assigned to tutors by load. You can reassign a review, but only tutors can approve or request changes.

step4.title: Maintain your profile
step4.description: Update your organization name, contact details, description, and logo in settings so certificates and the public page stay accurate.

q1.question: Who can review certificates?
q1.answer: Only tutors review. As an owner or representative you can assign or reassign reviews, but you cannot approve or request changes yourself.

q2.question: How do I add a tutor?
q2.answer: Invite the person or change an existing member role to tutor on the organization page. Reviews are then load-balanced across your tutors.

q3.question: Can I delete my organization?
q3.answer: Only the owner can delete an organization, and only when it has no certificates. Representatives have all other management rights.

q4.question: How do I join an organization?
q4.answer: You join through your organization. Someone from your organization invites you by email or shares an invite link, and some links need the organization's approval before you get in. If your organization is not on GloRe yet, a representative can apply to register it.

q5.question: I belong to more than one organization. How do I switch?
q5.answer: Use the organization switcher in the sidebar. Each organization is like a separate workspace, with its own courses, role, and certificates.

q6.question: Which languages are available?
q6.answer: The platform is available in English, Italian, and Spanish. You can switch language at any time from your account.

team.label: Team
team.intro: As a team member you author courses and, as an admin, manage organizations and users across the platform.

step1.title: Author courses
step1.description: Create and translate courses in the editor, with AI assistance for writing, improving, and summarizing content.

step2.title: Structure lessons
step2.description: Add lessons with rich text, questions, and self-assessment prompts. Skill courses end with a final assessment.

step3.title: Publish when ready
step3.description: A course becomes published, and visible to members, once every lesson has content. Use draft and partial states while you work.

step4.title: Manage the platform
step4.description: Admins approve organizations, moderate users, and invite team members from the admin panel. Editors focus on course content.

q1.question: When does a course become visible?
q1.answer: A course is published, and visible to members, once all of its lessons have content. Draft and partial states keep it hidden while you work.

q2.question: Who can edit courses?
q2.answer: Admins and editors edit courses. Everyone else sees them in viewer mode. Only admins reach the admin panel for organizations and users.

q3.question: What is the AI assistant?
q3.answer: The course editor includes AI commands to generate, improve, summarize, and translate content, plus inline copilot suggestions while you write.
